data.actual: Home / Products / Sulfate Process Titanium Dioxide Sulfate Process Titanium Dioxide Explore five Malaysia-origin titanium dioxide Grades currently classified as sulfate-process products. Use the process category to narrow the portfolio, then review each relevant Grade for your application, formulation and technical requirements. Explore Sulfate Grades · Request a Quote What the Sulfate Process Tells You At a general industrial level, the sulfate process treats titanium-bearing feedstock with sulfuric acid, followed by further steps that form and finish the TiO₂ pigment. “Sulfate” and “sulphate” are spelling variants for the same process category. The process label identifies a production route. It does not by itself establish the best Grade, application fit, performance, cost, environmental result or equivalence. Use each Grade's product information and your own formulation or process requirements to decide what to evaluate. General process reference: U.S. Federal Trade Commission public decision record. This reference describes the route at a general level; product details for the five Grades are provided on their individual pages. Source last reviewed: 6 September 2026. Explore Sulfate Grades Start with the Grades relevant to your application. Application needs can overlap, so open the individual product pages for product-specific information and compare only the candidates that fit your formulation and process. M-996 Documented for evaluation in industrial coatings, powder coatings, and exterior or interior architectural coatings. View M-996 M-2196 Documented for evaluation in solvent-based furniture and industrial paints. View M-2196 M-108 Documented for masterbatch and compounds, polyolefin and PVC film, and plastics requiring high thermal stability. View M-108 M-52 Documented for printing inks, can coatings and high-gloss interior architectural coatings. View M-52 M-2377 Documented for evaluation across coatings, plastics, masterbatch, printing inks and paper. View M-2377 The five entries are presented as evaluation candidates, without ranking or a guarantee of suitability. Confirm the selected Grade in your own formulation, processing, application and end-use conditions. Continue Your Evaluation Review by Application Use the application pages to organize your evaluation around the material system, formulation, processing conditions and end use. An application direction helps define what to test; it does not select a Grade automatically. Explore Applications Request Product Documents You can start a document request before deciding on a Grade, but choose one Product Grade before submitting. You may request several document types for that Grade. Evaluating more than one Grade? List the others in Additional Requirements for context. If you need different document types for each Grade, send a separate request for each one. Request Documents Compare Production Routes If you need a route-level comparison, use the separate guide. Grade selection still depends on product-specific evidence and testing in the intended application. Compare Chloride and Sulfate Routes Request a Quote If you have identified a Grade, select it on the quotation form. Otherwise, choose “Not sure / Need help”. Add other candidates and any non-confidential requirements in Additional Requirements, then provide your application, quantity in metric tonnes and destination. Request a Quote After you submit your quotation request, our team will review the details and contact you using the information provided.
